html:
Monitor workers and trigger flow

A monitor owns a finite command-observation session on one Gateway. It can create an ordinary Agent task when a condition matches. Its worker, observations and trigger receipt are separate from the resulting task's execution. The monitor user guide is authoritative for controls, defaults, condition syntax and current history limitations; this page follows the owners and messages behind those controls.

Creation and ownership

flowchart TD Explicit[Complete command and condition supplied by caller] --> Validate[Validate and normalize monitor specification] Draft[Explicit draft workflow] --> Proposal[Optional configured drafting model or local extraction] Proposal --> Validate Validate --> Definition[Persist command, finite timing and captured single-Gateway context] Definition --> Start[Explicit or create-time start] Start --> Manager[Manager lock and tracked worker handle] Manager --> Target[Resolve captured Gateway and terminal context] Target --> Sample[Repeated completed-command samples] Target --> Stream[One command with arriving stream events] Sample --> Observations[Stored observations and latest-observation pointer] Stream --> Observations Observations --> Readers[Inspection, paged history and SSE readers]

MonitorService injects the stores, Gateway client, target resolver, task starter and auxiliary model providers into one AgentMonitorManager. Initialization does not start a monitor. The manager owns live threads, cancellation events and judge cadence; the store owns definitions, observations, trigger receipts and the persisted native judge count.

The native start tool requires an actual command; drafting is an explicit separate workflow. Manager creation passes through validate_monitor_create, then persists the normalized definition before starting a worker. A later start failure does not erase that definition. Existing running work is reused. Archived monitors cannot start. Captured structured selection must contain one Gateway; it cannot silently widen to sibling targets.

Collecting evidence

sequenceDiagram participant M as Monitor manager participant G as Captured Gateway terminal participant E as Condition evaluator participant S as Monitor store M->>G: Open monitor-owned terminal M->>S: Mark running and retain terminal identity loop Until match, cooperative stop or duration boundary M->>S: Allocate sample sequence and save execution identity M->>G: Execute accepted command G-->>M: Collect stdout, stderr and exit status M->>E: Evaluate completed sample E-->>M: Match, reason and optional judge detail M->>S: Append observation and publish latest-observation pointer alt Condition matched M->>M: Handle trigger and leave sample loop else Continue observing M->>S: Clear current execution identity M->>M: Wait interval within remaining duration end end Note over M,G: A slow command can exceed the requested duration

Sample mode collects one command's output before evaluating it. Raw-stream mode uses one execution identity and evaluates each arriving event independently:

sequenceDiagram participant M as Streaming worker participant G as Gateway command stream participant E as Condition evaluator participant S as Monitor store M->>G: Start one command in the monitor terminal loop Each arriving event G-->>M: Output or status event alt Cancel requested or duration reached M->>G: Best-effort cancel recorded execution M->>M: Leave stream loop else Continue M->>E: Evaluate this event's text and supplied exit code E-->>M: Match and diagnostic detail M->>S: Append observation and latest pointer opt Condition matched M->>M: Handle trigger M->>G: Best-effort cancel command M->>M: Leave stream loop end end end

Streaming conditions do not combine text split across chunks, and a silent stream can delay deadline and cancellation checks. A completed event with no text is skipped by the raw worker. Shutdown returns without claiming completion and retains physical execution evidence for recovery. Ordinary worker failures inside the guarded loop record failed status and a notification; target-context resolution occurs before that guarded body, so its exceptions do not follow the same failure projection path.

Deciding whether a condition matched

flowchart TD Output[Sample or individual stream event] --> Mode{Trigger mode includes deterministic rules?} Mode -->|Yes| Rule[Evaluate configured contains, regex, numeric or exit rule] Rule -->|Matched| Match[Return match and evidence] Rule -->|Not matched| JudgeMode{Judged or hybrid mode with natural-language condition?} Mode -->|No| JudgeMode JudgeMode -->|No| Observe[Retain observation without trigger] JudgeMode -->|Yes| Gate{Judge enabled and cadence elapsed?} Gate -->|No| Observe Gate -->|Yes| Provider{Structured model client available?} Provider -->|No| Diagnostic[Record judge diagnostic and keep observing] Provider -->|Yes| Budget[For native model-led monitors, reserve persisted lifetime slot] Budget -->|Exhausted| Diagnostic Budget -->|Allowed| Call[Call configured judge with bounded output and schema] Call -->|Error or invalid result| Diagnostic Call -->|Valid| Confidence{should_trigger and confidence at least 0.5?} Confidence -->|Yes| Match Confidence -->|No| Observe

Hybrid evaluation tries deterministic matching first. A match avoids a judge call. The greater of global and monitor cadence controls attempts; cadence advances before provider availability is checked. Native model-led monitors reserve their lifetime slot before inference, and failed calls consume that slot. Judge errors or exhaustion do not stop observation collection.

Judge input combines a bounded history prefix with current output and keeps a character tail; it is not a full transcript or a query for the newest eight records. See the history limitations before interpreting that evidence. Model-returned task context is stored under monitor_judge_task_context, rather than merged into execution authority.

Trigger effects and independent tasks

sequenceDiagram participant M as Monitor manager participant T as Durable task owner participant S as Monitor store participant N as Notification store M->>S: Read current monitor after matched observation opt Action prompt and task store are available M->>T: Create task with captured single-Gateway scope and bounded evidence opt Task starter is configured M->>T: Queue or start through ordinary task admission end T-->>M: Task identity end M->>S: Mark triggered and link task identity M->>N: Create notification linked to monitor and observation N-->>M: Notification identity M->>S: Append trigger receipt linking observation, task and notification Note over T,N: Separate writes and callbacks allow earlier effects to survive a later failure

triggered records a matched condition and trigger handling. It cannot certify the action task's success. Missing action text or task storage produces no action task; the monitor can still publish a notification and trigger receipt. When a task is created, ordinary permission, admission, model and execution owners control its future work. Monitor deletion does not delete that task or its notifications.

Pause/cancel signals the local worker and best-effort cancels a recorded Gateway execution without joining the worker. Its returned lifecycle status is not proof of remote process death. Definition editing and deletion additionally reject a live worker and require the exact stored revision. Restart marks visible queued, running and paused monitors interrupted, preserving existing error reasons. It does not automatically restart commands or prove their external effects stopped.

The RAM monitor store publishes an observation and its latest pointer together; a standalone store uses its SQL transaction. Recovery checkpointing follows Controller state. Observation, trigger and SSE views are readers of retained state, not independent execution owners. The worker's bounded-prefix sequence allocation and summaries retain the limitations described in the user guide.
